title: Heterogeneous drying performance of a multi‐tier natural convection solar dryer
content:
Abstract

An innovative and cost-effective multi-tier cabinet solar dryer (MCSD) with an integrated stirring mechanism is presented to enhance drying efficiency under heterogeneous thermal conditions. Each cabinet functions as a flat plate solar collector, leveraging the greenhouse effect to minimize radiation and convection losses. The incorporation of an orientation mechanism optimizes solar energy intake, ensuring improved heat distribution. Developed in-house at PDPM IIITDM Jabalpur, the MCSD is durable, space-efficient, and portable, catering to marginal farmers and domestic users. The multi-tier design introduces heterogeneous drying conditions across different cabinets, leading to variable temperature and airflow patterns that facilitate diverse drying kinetics. The dryer showed a maximum thermal efficiency of 15.66% (batch) and 11.53% (continuous), with effective moisture diffusivity ranging from 2.204 × 10−10 (MCSD), 7.6549 × 10−10 (Single cabinet dryer) and 5.4636 × 10−10 (open sun drying) m2/s, a payback period of 0.68 years, and heat transfer coefficients of 15.07–17.84 W/m2·K across the cabinets. The designed configuration not only increases the overall drying capacity per unit space requirement, by approximately three times compared to a single-cabinet dryer (SCD) but also enables batch-mode drying to accommodate varying moisture removal rates. The study revealed that despite the heterogeneity in thermal profiles, a relatively uniform drying rate was achieved across all cabinets over three drying days, ensuring effective and consistent moisture reduction in vegetables, fruits, spices, and herbs under natural convection.
